name: M51-DS1
description: A cool supergiant in the Whirlpool Galaxy that dimmed more than sixfold and then recovered.

radius.source: Jencson et al. (2022), ApJ 930, 81, section 4.4.1: log(L/L_sun) = 5.60 for the best-fitting model (5.35 to 5.75 for the models that fit well, at the paper's distance modulus of M51, 29.67) and T_eff = 4300 K (3700 to 4700 K), through L = 4 pi R^2 sigma T^4 with the nominal solar 5772 K (IAU 2015 Resolution B3, Prsa et al. 2016, arXiv:1605.09788); the paper prints no radius, and no measurement of this star's size exists

temperature.source: Jencson et al. (2022), ApJ 930, 81, section 4.4.1: the model that best fits the star's light before its 2019 dimming has T_eff = 4300 K; the models that fit well span 3700 to 4700 K

gravityRange.source: Levesque et al. (2005), ApJ 628, 973, table 4 (the gravities it computes for the Galactic K- and M-type supergiants of known distance that it fits)

radialVelocity.source: SIMBAD's radial velocity of Whirlpool Galaxy, the star's galaxy, from 2022ApJS..261....6K; the star's own motion within the galaxy is not measured

distance.source: Placed in Whirlpool Galaxy as the app draws it, where the star's sight line crosses the disc's midplane: 8,341,566 pc (src/objects/m51-layers/source/recipe.json: centre 8,340,652 pc, inclination 32.6 deg, line of nodes 163 deg). The galaxy's distance, which places the galaxy and not a star within it: Tully et al. (2023), Cosmicflows-4, ApJ 944, 94; CDS J/ApJ/944/94, table 2 (distances of individual galaxies), PGC 47404: distance modulus 29.606 ± 0.079 mag (https://cdsarc.cds.unistra.fr/viz-bin/cat/J/ApJ/944/94)

position.credit: Jencson et al. (2022), ApJ 930, 81, section 4.1 (13:29:56.16 +47:11:47.8); SIMBAD holds that position, from 2022ApJ...930...81J

text.card: A cool supergiant in the Whirlpool Galaxy that dimmed more than sixfold by 2019 and then recovered.
text.introduction: Jencson et al. (2022) found it in a Hubble search for stars that vanish. Its light fits a star of 4,300 K, about 400,000 times as luminous as the Sun.
text.locator: abstract (the dimming and the rebrightening); section 4.4.1: T_eff, log(L/L_sun)

notes: The star varies; it is drawn at the radius its published luminosity and temperature give
Its radius is not measured: it follows from the paper's luminosity and temperature
The paper also allows a cooler red supergiant, under 3,700 K at log L 5.2 to 5.3, if less dust lies in front of the star
Its limb is read at the gravities published for Galactic K and M supergiants; no gravity of this star is measured
Its radial velocity is its galaxy's; its own motion within M51 is not measured
